# Queue Overloaded

`customer_support.sit.queue_overloaded` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `customer_support.support_operations.queue_management`


> A queue is taking in more than it is getting through, and has been for long enough that the oldest end of it has stopped being served at all. Not a busy morning — a rate mismatch that has persisted, which is a different thing with different remedies. The characteristic shape is a queue that looks acceptable by count and terrible by age distribution: the middle of the queue moves, the tail calcifies, and every incentive an individual agent has points away from the tail. The situation is about the team's ability to absorb what arrives, so the useful questions are what changed on the arrival side, what is deliberately not being served while this is true, and who has been forgotten — never simply how many are open.

> Every string in signals_of_progress and signals_of_decay is a support-native obs kind from planned_substrate; none is emitted today, and none is schema-validated, so the file loads without being able to run. This situation is further from executable than any other in the domain — both of its objects, Queue and Backlog, are planned rather than authored, and its core measure, derived.backlog_age, is a planned fact path. agent_reassigned appears under progress here and under decay in escalation-requested.yaml. That is not an inconsistency: moving people onto a drowning queue is the correct response at this altitude, and moving a single escalated customer between owners is the failure at that one. It is a good illustration of why obs kinds cannot be scored globally and have to be read inside a situation. ticket_closed sits under progress and should be read with suspicion by any reviewer. Bulk closure of aged tickets is the most common cosmetic response to this exact situation: it removes the symptom, keeps the demand, and returns within a fortnight as reopens and repeat contacts. ticket_reopened is in the decay list partly as the counterweight to it, and the pair should be read together or not at all.
